faq.a: Abduljabbar represents Arabic عَبْدُ الْجَبَّار, meaning servant of the Compeller/All-Powerful.

faq.q: What is the origin of Abduljabbar?
faq.a: The name is Arabic and is a compound of عبد and a second element.
Yes. The underlying compound is عَبْدُ الْجَبَّار (ʿAbd al-Jabbār).

faq.q: What is the root of Abduljabbar?
faq.a: عبد is related to ع ب د; al-Jabbār is related to ج ب ر (j-b-r).
Abduljabbar is a traditional Muslim personal name because it contains a compound invoking al-Jabbār, a divine epithet in Islamic tradition.
This record does not establish Abduljabbar as an explicitly named Qur'anic person; the compound's religious meaning is distinct from personal-name attestation in the text.

faq.q: What does Abduljabbar mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, the name means servant of the Compeller/All-Powerful; the compound combines عبد with al-Jabbār.
The supplied “ab-dul-jab-bar” is an approximate pronunciation; local pronunciations vary.

faq.q: Is Abduljabbar a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: The record classifies the name as masculine, consistent with traditional usage; regional frequency data is not supplied.
